transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah… good to meet you too. I guess I came in because people have been noticing I’m… moving differently, I guess. Sometimes I’m really slowed down, like I’m underwater—taking forever to answer someone or even just get up from a chair. And other times I’m kind of the opposite, pacing around my apartment and rubbing my hands, like I’m trying to shake off a bad call from work. It’s probably not as dramatic as it sounds, but it’s been obvious enough that I figured I should talk to someone.
Have you been feeling depressed معظم اليوم nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s been kind of hanging around most days for a long time—like a little over two years now. Maybe about two years and a month. It lets up here and there for short stretches, but it doesn’t really stay gone.
Have you ever had a manic episode?

Um… I don’t think so? I mean, I’ve had times where I’m restless or maybe not acting totally like myself, but I’m not sure if that’s what you mean by manic. I wouldn’t want to say yes if it doesn’t really fit. Could you maybe explain what you’re looking for?
Have you ever had a period when you felt so unusually energized or wired that it was clearly different from your normal self?

I’m not sure I’d call it “unusually energized,” exactly. I’ve had times where I’m keyed up or restless, but I don’t know that it was like… clearly a different version of me, if that makes sense. Maybe I’m not describing it right, but I don’t want to overstate it.
Have you ever heard voices when no one else was there?

Um… yeah, a little. I mean, not like full conversations or anything. Sometimes I’ll hear the old headset beep, or like a supervisor-type voice saying my name… or “too slow,” even when my laptop’s closed and there’s no phone ringing. I know that sounds strange.
Do you ever hear that voice at times when you are not feeling depressed?

Yeah… I think so. Not all the time, and I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but there have been stretches where I wasn’t really depressed—like a few weeks where I felt more normal, was keeping up with things—and I’d still hear that supervisor-type voice sometimes. Or I’d get this strong feeling like the old ticketing software was flagging me, even though I knew that didn’t really make sense. Does that answer what you mean?
Have the voice and the feeling that the software was flagging you ever lasted for at least two weeks during a time when you were not depressed?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, because I was functioning pretty okay, but there were stretches of a few weeks where my mood was more normal and I was getting things done, and I’d still hear that supervisor voice sometimes. And I’d still get that feeling like the old ticketing software was flagging me, even though I wasn’t really depressed then. Does that count as what you’re asking?
During this time, have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but the low mood has been there for a long time—like a little over two years now. It eases up here and there, but only for short stretches. Most of the time, yeah, I’ve had periods where I felt depressed most of the day, pretty much every day for at least a couple weeks. Does that make sense?
Over these past two years, have the voice and the feeling that the software was flagging you been present for most of that time?

Yeah… I guess, yes. Not literally every day, but they’ve been around for a long while—maybe about a year and eight months or so. And it wasn’t only when I was at my worst mood-wise. Even when the sadness wasn’t as heavy, I’d still sometimes hear the voice or get that feeling like the software was tracking or flagging me. I don’t know if “most of the time” is the right way to say it, but it’s been a pretty consistent thing over that stretch.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least four days when you felt unusually up or irritable compared with your normal self?

I don’t think so… not for four days straight. I mean, I can get irritated or have a better day here and there, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had a stretch where I was unusually up or not myself like that. At least, nothing that really stands out to me.
